scenarios.title: Build a kernel with root-driver support
scenarios.summary: Repair a source configuration and verify image, modules and early-userspace inputs.
scenarios.objective: Build the supplied target image with external initramfs-loading support and working NVMe/ext4 root-driver support. Keep the saved configuration and build inputs consistent; a modular repair or supported built-in alternative may satisfy the task.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read each failed outcome. Compare saved versus draft settings, source/release identity and actual virtual paths before retrying.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: A saved configuration, its outputs and installed files are separate states.
guide.action: Read the introduction and worked example, then investigate the supplied workspace.

guide.title: Explore the separate example
guide.why: Saved inputs, build outputs and staged files can disagree after an edit.
guide.action: Use the worked values in the separate example; inspect the actual output and retry a changed setting.

guide.title: Check the independent assignment
guide.why: A successful build command alone does not prove all required outcomes.
guide.action: Complete the supplied assignment and select Check configuration or Check build; use each failed outcome to repair the state.

scenarios.explanation: A configuration is an input, not a rebuilt image. Save supported root-driver choices, then build the target source. Built-in drivers are part of the image; loadable root drivers also need matching module inputs and early userspace. Changing a configuration or source does not update earlier build records.
hints: Compare the saved configuration with the draft before rebuilding.
A loadable root driver needs matching module inputs and early userspace.
Try both supported driver strategies: built-in, or modules with a matching initramfs.
scenarios.simplifications: Checked2026-11-16local/17UTC; LPIC-2 v4.5 objective201.2, narrow practical subset only. Five-setting supplied configuration, fixed NVMe/ext4 baseline, typed build records and virtual staging. No actual compilation, Kconfig dependency evaluation, arbitrary Makefile/recipes, DKMS, firmware or real boot. Native staging/initramfs controls are simulator helpers. Supported literal make subset is documented in KERNEL_BUILD_SUBSET.md. UUID boot uses supplied early userspace. No host files, processes or network.

scenarios.title: Stage a new kernel beside a working fallback
scenarios.summary: Keep a working recovery path while staging and verifying a different kernel build.
scenarios.objective: Stage a working boot candidate from the supplied target source, using the saved configuration and a new loader-entry filename. Use the supplied system-root identity. Preserve every original fallback image, module tree, initramfs and entry unchanged. Verify a new-kernel boot through root and init handoff; booting the old fallback alone is insufficient.

scenarios.explanation: Build outputs, installed files and loader selections are different states. The candidate must select a staged image from the requested source and current configuration. A matching release label alone is not sufficient. Matching early userspace supplies root-driver modules and UUID lookup; the original fallback must remain available unchanged.
hints: Compare the saved configuration with the draft before rebuilding.
A loadable root driver needs matching module inputs and early userspace.
Use actual virtual file paths and retain the working fallback.
